depth_findings.text: Nothing writes the executor markers on round folds yet, so with SESSION_CORE_CRASH_PARK_ENABLED on the worker refuses every fold as route_unrecorded; the executor must write parks-so-far (a resumed run's count too, or the park cap is bypassed), route model, connection id and child ceiling on round folds of run_parkable loops only, and never on an approval continuation or client/MCP-tool run, or crash-park holds runs nothing can resume for the 24 h TTL.

Zombie loop: a loop silent for more than the 15 min deadline plus the 15 min grace is crash parked and can then be continued while still alive; its later fold save goes stale and the writer fails but the loop keeps going (read-only calls, final answer), so two loops can answer one run; the thread watermark only catches an answer already appended, so the executor must stop a run_parkable loop at its first stale/closed save before any further inference, append or receipt.

No UI or button resumes a park, so with crash park on a dead run is now held up to SESSION_CORE_PARK_TTL_SECONDS (default 86400) with no thread explanation instead of ending outcome_unknown at about 15 min; the owner has to decide the TTL (or a fixed notice) before flip (4).

The S8-B go-ahead and design are open owner decisions in the ledger (three design reviews found critical defects in the earlier designs); this half follows the v4 invariants that fit the owned files (marker-gated, grace plus heartbeat push, thread lock, watermark re-check at claim) but has not had its own independent review.

The park_crashed SQL, the claim re-check, the SKIP LOCKED thread lock and the heartbeat push are source-verified only; none ran against Postgres (five ignored DB tests written), and the live proof (docker kill execution-core past the deadline, park_not_due, resume by continue, TTL expiry) needs the executor half first.

THREAD_WATERMARK_KEY, the 900 s grace and the round-budget defaults (12, 32) are session-core-local copies; move them to mp-contracts::loop_fold so execution-core, session-core and the tests share one definition and a source guard can pin them.

No mutation campaign was run on the new refusal rules; the DB tests cover each unsafe-fact case once but not a concurrent append racing park_crashed, nor a crash park claimed by two continuations (the existing claim lease covers it by construction).

A crash park writes CHECKPOINT_SAVED but emits no RunParked event or run_parked frame (nobody is alive to emit it); RunDetail.park_reason will read crash_interrupted, so decide whether the run console should show a crash park and whether the gateway's park form wording fits a park the user never saw start.

save() re-serializes the round fold through serde_json::Value to stamp it while crash parking is on, which reorders keys and drops nothing today; fold_digest remains the digest of the executor's bytes, not the sealed plaintext, so any future consumer of fold_digest must not assume they match.

Lock order: the answer-append path locks threads before runs while the worker and claim hold runs first; both new thread reads use FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED so they never wait, but a busy thread makes a claim retry (loop_checkpoint_claim_held) and the worker retry in 60 s, which a hot thread could prolong.

The thread_watermark stamp lives in fold extensions and is carried forward by any resume that clones the fold, so a later executor-written park fold (credential window, provider exhausted) on a crash-resumed run keeps the old stamp; claim() keys its thread re-check on the stamp alone, so it would close that legitimate park when the thread has moved since, ending the run outcome_unknown. Strip the key when the executor writes a park fold, or key the claim re-check on park_reason crash_interrupted, before the switch is flipped.

Executor markers are not written on round folds, so with SESSION_CORE_CRASH_PARK_ENABLED on every fold is refused route_unrecorded; the executor must write the four park keys (including a resumed run's park count) on run_parkable round folds only, never on approval continuations or client/MCP-tool runs.

Zombie loop: a loop silent past the 15 min deadline plus the 15 min grace can be crash parked and continued while still alive, so two loops could answer one run; the executor must stop at its first stale or closed fold save before any further inference, append or receipt.

With crash park on, a dead run is held up to SESSION_CORE_PARK_TTL_SECONDS (default 86400) with no thread explanation and no UI to resume it, instead of ending outcome_unknown after about 15 min; owner must pick the TTL or a fixed notice before flip (4).

results.notes:
S8-A (executor park, resume, run_parked frame, RunParked 24 / RunResumed 25, chat-client minimal handling, TTL expiry, parked/resuming spare) was already built and live-proven. This pass built the SESSION-CORE HALF of S8-B (crash-park) behind SESSION_CORE_CRASH_PARK_ENABLED (default off, strict parser, also needs the fold store and SESSION_CORE_PARK_RECOVERY_ENABLED). With it off, behaviour is the committed one: save() adds no stamp, the worker takes no new branch and the heartbeat pushes nothing.

What was built. loop_checkpoint.rs: (1) save() stamps a round fold with `thread_watermark` (the thread's highest message sequence) only while crash parking is on; (2) `park_crashed` runs inside the worker's transaction and re-seals an ACTIVE round fold as a `crash_interrupted` park at seq+1 with park_until = now()+900 s, only when persistent, no open approval, no open ledger reservation and no ledger row newer than the fold, the thread unmoved since the stamp (read under the thread lock, SKIP LOCKED so it never deadlocks with the answer-append path, which locks threads before runs), and the fold passes the same structural rules the executor's check_park_fold applies on resume (system message first, ledger flag, authority digest, no open round, no pending pause, no Space, park cap, round budget left, route keys and non-zero child ceiling); (3) claim() of a crash park re-checks the thread under its lock and closes the fold when it moved (keyed on the stamp, so it holds after the switch is turned off); (4) `push_crash_park` for the heartbeat. terminalization.rs: the switch and its test override, `try_crash_park` in recover_claimed_terminalization (parked runs go back to their obligation like any park; a busy thread releases the run for 60 s; anything refused takes the committed outcome_unknown path), and the heartbeat push of a crash park's park_until (never moves updated_at, the TTL anchor).

WHY PARTIAL. The executor half cannot be built from the owned files and the design still has open points: (a) the executor must write the four park keys (parks so far, route model, connection id, child ceiling) on its ROUND folds when run_parkable, and today durable_loop_contract.rs and park.rs pin those keys to park_fold only, so that needs park.rs and an amended guard (neither owned); until it lands every fold is refused `route_unrecorded` and the worker never parks anything (inert, byte-identical); (b) the zombie stop needs a FoldWriter accessor (fold.rs) and agent.rs; (c) the 2026-10-20 ledger entry says crash-park was split off after three design reviews and the S8-B go-ahead and design are OWNER decisions, and flip (4) is owner-gated. Plan section 4.4 reserves no migration for S8 (0049 is taken by thread_activity_cursor), so I used no migration: the watermark rides in the encrypted fold's extensions instead of a column.

results.notes:
The slice's code is built, with the new behaviour reachable only when a thread is explicitly set to off. No new env switch was added: the row has no flag, and every thread defaults to 'inherit'. MEMORY_CONTROLS_ENABLED=false also disables the thread check.

What changed:
- Migration 0067_thread_memory_mode.sql adds threads.memory_mode TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'inherit' with a CHECK on ('inherit','off'), added NOT VALID then validated. The revert file is revert/0067_thread_memory_mode.down.sql. Number 0067 is the next free after the plan's section 4.4 reservations, which run to 0066. The plan only says "next free if scheduled".
- sessions.proto: `optional string memory_mode = 10` on UpdateThreadPresentationRequest. Tags 7, 8 and 9 are already taken (WS17 S7 and archived), so 10 is the next free tag on that message. The change is additive only.
- memory_control.rs adds ThreadMemoryMode (inherit|off, with a strict from_wire), MemoryReason::ThreadOff (wire token "thread_off"), and apply_thread_mode. apply_thread_mode makes a thread set off deny everything, org rows included. A denial that already leaves nothing readable (ZDR, org policy) keeps its own reason. It also adds resolve_for_thread (reader, takes the pool) and resolve_in_tx_for_thread (writer, taken under the user row lock). permits_extraction now also refuses messages of a thread set off, so the Dreaming persist paths are covered without editing dreaming.rs.
- grpc.rs: append_message_in_tx and load_context_memory_rows now use the thread-aware gate. update_thread_presentation accepts memory_mode. It rejects any value except "inherit" or "off", and refuses a ZDR caller with DURABLE_MUTATION_FORBIDDEN. It also takes the user's memory row lock before commit so an extraction in flight is ordered against the change. The THREAD_PRESENTATION_UPDATED event payload records the mode.
- The ignored Postgres test thread_off_blocks_read_and_write_for_that_thread_only is in grpc.rs's persona_db_tests module. It compiled but has not been run.

results.notes:
The cap numbers stay at today's 1 MB, so every default is byte-identical, and the OD18 ruling is a config flip (DEC-37).

FE handoff: pending-chat-launch.ts no longer puts attachment data URLs in sessionStorage. The sessionStorage envelope (text and metadata) keeps the 2,000,000-char cap, with each attachment's url replaced by an idb:<id> reference. The bytes go to IndexedDB (non-ZDR only) and the full launch stays in memory for same-tab navigation. ZDR launches are memory-only and never open IndexedDB. If IndexedDB is blocked the write rejects with PendingChatLaunchError('storage') and nothing is truncated. consumePendingChatLaunch() stays synchronous, so it serves memory launches and launches without attachments. A reloaded launch whose bytes sit in IndexedDB is left in place until the new consumePendingChatLaunchAsync() restores it. That function returns null, not a launch missing a file, if the bytes are gone.

prepare-chat-attachments.ts now reads the per-file limit from getAttachmentPolicy()?.maxFileBytes, falling back to ATTACHMENT_MAX_FILE_BYTES, and names the limit in the Norwegian refusal text.

Body limits: BFF streams.rs and model-gateway http_routes.rs each derive the stream body limit as max(explicit limit, base64(CHAT_ATTACHMENT_MAX_TOTAL_BYTES) + 4 MiB). The 12 MiB default is unchanged. Both read the same two env names.

Tonic limits: inference-core's 16 MiB decode limit and a new execution-core decode limit are now max(16 MiB, CHAT_ATTACHMENT_MAX_TOTAL_BYTES + 8 MiB). Execution-core had no decode limit before; the field it will carry arrives with S5/S6.

imports-core: chat_extract.py reads CHAT_EXTRACT_MAX_BYTES (strict positive integer, default 1,000,000). It derives the base64 field cap as bytes*7//5 (1,400,000 at the default) and puts the limit in the 413 message. The 60,000-char limit and the zip guard are untouched. The new pytest cases reload the module with a 4 MB cap and cover default unchanged, bad values keep the default, the 60k text limit holds under the raised cap, a file over the cap is refused, and the zip bomb is still refused under the raised cap.
